sections.h2: Three ways to sell a Minnetonka house fast
sections.html:
A Minnetonka owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept cash from a buyer who takes the house as it stands. The cash route fits best when repairs are pending, tenants are in place, or the closing date cannot slide.

Every route runs through the same paperwork. The parcel is in Hennepin County, so the county bills the tax and files the deed. Minnetonka also keeps its own assessor, so a value question goes to city hall instead of the county offices downtown.

Most Minnetonka households own, and values run high. About 28 percent of homes are rentals, and 88.2 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, so turnover is modest. The 2025 population estimate is 53,969.

Three school districts cover the city: Hopkins in the central and eastern part, Minnetonka in the west, and Wayzata along the northern edge. Name the district in your listing description, since the answer shifts from one street to the next.

Minnetonka requires registration for every rental property, however short the stay. The ordinance was adopted on December 18, 2023 and took effect on February 3, 2024. Each certificate lapses one year after submission, and renewal notices arrive by email.

  • Condo and townhome owners name the unit being rented.
  • Single-family houses, duplexes and triplexes need one application per unit.
  • The designated property manager must be able to respond in person when something goes wrong.

The council passed a short-term rental ordinance on June 8, 2026. Stays under 30 days now require both a registration and a homestead, so only an occupant who treats the home as a primary residence may rent all or part of it. An investor reading your listing will weigh that limit. Request the ordinance text from the city before telling anyone that a short-term use is permitted.

sections.h2: What Minnesota requires a Minnetonka seller to put in writing
sections.html:
Residential sellers owe the buyer a written disclosure before any agreement is signed, as Minnesota Statutes section 513.55 directs. You must name each material fact you know of that would significantly and adversely affect how an ordinary buyer uses and enjoys the home. Write it honestly and from what you actually know. Handing it to the buyer's licensee counts as delivery, and the licensee can pass it on.

A few records make the form easier to complete.

  • Older building permits, which sit in the city's records archive.
  • The location of property stakes and buried utility lines, which residents can trace with a metal detector borrowed from the city.
  • Anything you know about water, drainage or foundation trouble near the creek or the lake shore.

New permit applications, payments and plan reviews all happen online. Phone 952-939-8394 to learn how long a review is running before an open permit delays your closing.

sections.h2: Hennepin County taxes and a Minnetonka sale
sections.html:
Tax bills split into two payments, May 15 and October 15. When a due date falls on a weekend or holiday, you get until the next business day. The next first-half date, May 15, 2027, is a Saturday, so the payment moves to Monday, May 17.

Questions about your value or classification go to the city assessor at 952-939-8220. The county fixes values as of January 2 and mails notices in March. April and May are the window for informal talks. A formal appeal begins at the local board. Next is the county board of appeal and equalization in mid-June, and Minnesota Tax Court is the other formal route.

  • E-check payments online carry no fee. Cards, PayPal and Venmo add a service charge.
  • A check sent by mail needs a postmark no later than the due date.
  • To pay in person, go to the Government Center at 300 South 6th Street, 6th floor, on a weekday. A drop box on that floor accepts checks through the early evening.
  • Lender escrow folds the taxes into the mortgage payment, so a new owner may never see the bill.

Three notices arrive each year. The valuation notice comes in March, the proposed levies notice in November, and the tax statement in March with payment stubs. The November estimate leaves out special assessments that may be added to the final bill, and it gives the dates of the truth-in-taxation meetings where residents can comment on budgets.

Hennepin County will erase a late-payment penalty one time in any ten years, and only on the current year's taxes. The application deadline is June 30 for a first-half payment and November 30 for a second-half payment, and the full tax must already be paid. Clear any older balance on the parcel before you set a closing date, because it blocks the request.

sections.h2: A step-by-step order for a quick Minnetonka sale
sections.html: Begin with the paperwork you control: older permits from the city archive and a finished disclosure statement. For a rental, check that the registration is current and explain to the buyer what happens to the tenants. Next, collect cash offers and compare the closing date, the check amount and each closing line. Pick one, sign, and let the buyer order title work. At closing the deed goes to Hennepin County for recording, and any unpaid tax or special assessment is paid from the proceeds. Keep the tax statement and your last payment receipt handy so the title company sees what is owed and what is paid.

sections.h2: What to ask before taking a cash offer
sections.html:
Get the proposal on paper, showing the closing date, the check amount, and who covers each closing line. A company buying in present condition should say whether it plans any repairs, and you should be equally direct about what you know of the house.

  • Does the offer depend on an inspection or on financing?
  • Who orders the title search, and who pays recording charges?
  • If tenants live there, what becomes of their lease?
  • May you stay a couple of weeks after closing to finish moving?

A quick sale still needs the disclosure statement, a deed and a trip to the county recorder. What it removes is months of showings. Set the cash figure beside what a listing would net after repairs, commissions, and the months of mortgage, insurance and utilities you would carry. Then pick the route that matches your calendar.

faqs.q: Does a Minnetonka landlord need to keep the registration active during a sale?
faqs.a: Yes, while tenants live there. The city registers every rental regardless of length, and a certificate lasts one year. Renew before the expiration printed on it.

faqs.q: Who sets my Minnetonka house's value for tax purposes?
faqs.a: The city assessor, reachable at 952-939-8220, and not the county office. Hennepin County still collects the money and holds the county appeal board in mid-June.

faqs.q: When does the next Hennepin County tax payment come due?
faqs.a: The first half is due May 15, 2027. That is a Saturday, which moves the deadline to Monday, May 17, and the second half follows on October 15.

faqs.q: Can my buyer run short-term rentals out of the house?
faqs.a: Only as an owner living there. The June 8, 2026 ordinance requires a homestead and a city registration for any stay under 30 days.

faqs.q: Can a late tax penalty be removed in Hennepin County?
faqs.a: Sometimes. The county allows one abatement every ten years, for current-year taxes. The second-half deadline is November 30, and you must first pay the tax in full, with nothing left over from earlier years.
